title: Youvetsi
subtitle: Greek braised beef and orzo baked in a clay pot
excerpt: Beef cooked slowly in a rich tomato and cinnamon sauce with orzo pasta, all baked together until the orzo has absorbed the braising liquid and the meat falls apart. A warming, deeply savoury bake.
sourceNotes: Traditional Greek dish, the name coming from the clay pot it is classically baked in. Widely eaten across Greece as a Sunday family meal.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Braise the beef a day ahead and refrigerate in its sauce. Add the orzo and finish in the oven on the day.

content.text: Youvetsi is comfort food built on patience. The beef needs a long, gentle braise before the orzo goes in, or the pasta will be overcooked by the time the meat is tender. Watch the liquid level carefully; the orzo drinks it fast.
Heat the oven to 180C. Heat the olive oil in the dutch oven over a high heat. Season the beef. Brown it in two batches, 3 minutes per side, then set aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the red wine. Stir and let it bubble for 2 minutes to reduce slightly. Add the tinned tomatoes, 600ml of the stock, the cinnamon stick, bay leaves, allspice, salt, and pepper.
Return the beef to the pot. Bring to a simmer, then cover and transfer to the oven. Braise for 2 hours until the beef is very tender.
Remove the cinnamon stick and bay leaves. Stir the dry orzo into the pot with the remaining 200ml of stock. The liquid should just cover the orzo. Push the beef chunks down among the pasta.
Return to the oven uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the orzo is tender and has absorbed most of the liquid. Rest for 10 minutes. Serve with grated parmesan.

items.symptom: The orzo is glued together in a solid mass.
items.cause: Too little liquid or the pot was not stirred during the orzo bake.
items.fix: Stir once after 12 minutes in the oven and add a splash of hot stock if it looks dry.

items.symptom: The beef is still tough after 2 hours.
items.cause: The braise was not at a gentle enough simmer, or the cut was too lean.
items.fix: Return the covered pot to the oven for another 30 minutes. Chuck needs a proper low heat to break down.

items.cause: Not enough browning on the beef, or the wine was omitted.
items.fix: Proper caramelisation on the beef is where the depth comes from. Don't rush the browning stage.
